questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

She might have completed her research by that time.

options.text: Her research might be completed by her by that time.
Her research might had been completed by her by that time.
Her research might have been completed by her by that time.
Her research might have completed by her by that time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Her research might have been completed by her by that time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To covert an active voice to the passive voice, we need to follow the **rules**:

 
 
• Identify the subject, verb, and object.
 
• Move the object to the beginning of the sentence.
 
• Use the appropriate form of the verb based on the original verb tense.
 
• Use the past participle form of the main verb.
 
 
 
• The sentence is in the active voice with "**She**" as the **subject **and "**completed**" as the **verb**.
 
• To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object (**research**) the subject and use the past participle form of the verb (**completed**).
 
• The helping verb "**might have**" remains unchanged in the passive voice sentence.
 
• The preposition "**by**" is used to indicate the doer of the action (her) in the passive voice sentence.
 
• So, it is clear that only the sentence written in option 3 follows all the rules.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: **Incorrect **- This sentence is in active voice and has the same subject and verb as the original sentence.
 
• Option 2: **Incorrect **- The use of "had been" is unnecessary and incorrect in this sentence.
 
• Option 4: **Incorrect **- The verb "completed" needs to be in the past participle form for passive voice, which is missing in this option.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

She always / invite me / to / dinner.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **invite me**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This error lies in the subject-verb agreement, where the verb does not agree with the subject in terms of number.
 
• **Subject-verb agreement** means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or both plural.
 
• A singular subject takes a singular verb. A plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• So, the correct verb form should be "**invites**" instead of "**invite**" to match the subject "**She**".

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *She always invites me to dinner.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**She always**" is grammatically correct.
 
• "**to**" is a preposition and is used correctly in the sentence.
 
• "**dinner**" is a noun and is used correctly in the sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

By whom was the coffee made?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Who made the coffee?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In active voice, the subject of the sentence performs the action.
 
• To convert a passive sentence to an active voice, we need to identify the **subject **of the passive sentence and make it the **doer **of the action.
 
• In this sentence, "**coffee**" is the subject in passive voice and "**made**" is the verb.
 
• We need to change the sentence to "Who made the coffee?" to make it an active voice.
 
• The doer of the action (the person who made the coffee) becomes the subject of the sentence in an active voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Correct active voice:** *Who made the coffee?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "**Who had made the coffee?**" is in the past perfect tense and suggests that the coffee was made before some other past event.
 
• Option 3: "**Who has made the coffee?**" is in the present perfect tense and suggests that the coffee was made recently.
 
• Option 4: "**Who makes the coffee?**" is also in active voice but is in present tense instead of past tense like the original sentence.
